brief: A 6-second title card for a podcast called 'Signal & Noise': the title types on letter by letter over a dark gradient, then a thin waveform line animates underneath.
checks: The on‑screen text reads exactly "Signal & Noise" (including the ampersand and spaces).
The background behind the title is a dark gradient (not a solid color or a light area).
The title appears by typing each letter sequentially, with no letters appearing all at once.
The typing animation finishes before any waveform line becomes visible.
A thin horizontal line (the waveform) appears beneath the title after the typing finishes.
The waveform line’s height is noticeably smaller than the height of a capital letter in the title.
The waveform line animates (e.g., draws from left to right or pulses) after it appears.
The waveform animation completes and the line remains visible for at least the final half‑second of the card.
No part of the text or waveform touches or crosses the outer edge of the frame.
The title text is large enough to be easily readable (≈ 1/10 of the frame height) and has high contrast against the dark gradient.
Both the typing and waveform animations use ease‑in/ease‑out curves rather than moving at a constant speed.
There is some visual change in every second of the video (no dead‑air intervals).
The first half‑second contains visible animation (nothing is completely static before 0.5 s).
The final composition holds still for at least 0.5 seconds before the video ends.
